scope: Typed DSD software ownership and failed-close evidence. No public DSD submission or physical qualification.
behavior: One typed PCM, DSD, or network observation preserves existing PCM wire fields.
DSD source bits remain distinct from carrier frames.
Cancellation and takeover retain the original failed-close error and accepted prefix under the old identity.
Host adoption and current terminal adoption use distinct acknowledgements.
Queue backpressure and failed diagnostic writes retain bounded evidence.
limits: The final worker binary belongs to its isolated source; integrated binaries need fresh provenance.
Scripted close failures prove ownership bookkeeping, not native stop-error physics.
Unwritten diagnostics remain nondurable through host lifetime only.
Public DSD Unmute remains blocked by endpoint qualification.
Older service IPC deadline failures remain retained; unchanged repeated services and final focused services passed.
